dossier.public_summary: This dip is not a planet. The detected dips alternate between deep and shallow at half the 11.1-day period, and two of the 12 transits are much deeper while two others vanish. Depths also change dramatically between sectors. Together this matches a blended eclipsing binary, not a steady small-planet transit.

reasons.why: Odd and even depths differ strongly (>3 and depth ratio 3.2), typical of an eclipsing binary at twice the period (22.2 d). Sector odd/even also divergent.
Individual transit depths are completely inconsistent. Two transits dominate the entire signal with depths ~3x the mean, while two subsequent transits show near-zero (negative) depths.
